ov: A wild camelid of the high Andes and probably the ancestor of the alpaca. It grows small amounts of extremely fine wool; the Inca let only royalty wear it. Hunting cut numbers to about 6,000 by 1974, but the population has recovered to about 350,000.
rg: The central Andes of Peru, northwestern Argentina, Bolivia and northern Chile, at 3,200–4,800 m; introduced to Ecuador.

cf.tip: The vicuña is the wild animal the domestic alpaca is believed to come from.

fx: It is the national animal of Peru and appears on the Peruvian coat of arms.
Its fibres are 12 micrometres across, finer than cashmere’s 14.
